outcome: Short-term variation (STV) in fetal heart rate
cohort: The study included 628 singleton pregnancies with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM), delivering between 24+0 to 33+6 gestational weeks.
finding: Fetuses exposed to Intraamniotic infection (IAI) showed a significantly steeper decline in their short-term variation (STV) in fetal heart rate during the last 24 hours before labor and an increased baseline fetal heart rate frequency in the last 12 hours before labor compared to those not exposed.
